'''Juan Felipe Cucker Farkas''' (born 1958) is an [[Uruguayans|Uruguayan]] mathematician and [[theoretical computer scientist]] who has done research into the [[computational complexity theory|complexity theory]] of the [[Blum–Shub–Smale machine|Blum–Shub–Smale computational model]] and the [[computational complexity|complexity]] of [[numerical algorithm]]s in [[linear programming]] and [[numerical algebraic geometry]].

== Biography ==

Cucker was born in [[Montevideo]] in 1958.<ref name="arbol">{{cite web|url=https://www.arbolmat.com/juan-felipe-cucker-farkas/|title=JUAN FELIPE CUCKER FARKAS|website=Árbol de las Matemáticas|date=1 November 2016|access-date=2020-10-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200804114016/https://www.arbolmat.com/juan-felipe-cucker-farkas/|archive-date=2020-08-04|language=es}} Also: {{cite web|url=http://www.rsme.es/arbolmat/Cucker/Cucker-Dossier.html|title=Dossier de Felipe Cucker|website=Árbol de las Matemáticas|date=1 November 2016|access-date=2020-10-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201004212949/http://www.rsme.es/arbolmat/Cucker/Cucker-Dossier.html|publisher=[[Royal Spanish Mathematical Society]]|archive-date=2020-10-04|language=es}}</ref><ref name="interview">{{citation|url=https://www.scmp.com/magazines/post-magazine/article/1323464/my-life-felipe-cucker|title=My life: Felipe Cucker|access-date=2020-10-02|date=6 October 2013|first1=Sarah|last1=Lazarus|website=Post Magazine|publisher=[[South China Morning Post]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180619163114if_/http://www.scmp.com/magazines/post-magazine/article/1323464/my-life-felipe-cucker|archive-date=2018-06-19}}.</ref><ref name="biography">{{cite web|url=http://felipesfest.github.io/felipecucker.html|title=Biography of Felipe Cucker|access-date=2020-10-02|first1=Peter|last1=Bürgisser|author1-link=Peter Bürgisser|website=Complexity of numerical computation: A conference in honor of Felipe Cucker}}</ref> Due to the situation in Uruguay in the 70s, he emigrated to Spain to study the [[bachelor's degree|bachelor]] of mathematics at the [[University of Barcelona]],<ref name="interview"/><ref name="biography"/> which he completed in 1983. He obtained his PhD degree at the [[University of Cantabria]] and [[University of Rennes 1]] in 1986 under the supervision Tomás Recio and Michel Coste. His thesis was about [[Nash functions]] on real [[algebraic variety|algebraic varieties]].<ref name="arbol"/><ref>{{MathGenealogy|37090|Juan Felipe Cucker Farkas}}</ref>

From 1987 to 1992 Cucker was professor at the [[Polytechnic University of Catalonia]].<ref name="arbol"/><ref name="biography"/>

In 1992 Cucker became professor at the recently created [[Pompeu Fabra University]].<ref name="biography"/> In 1995 he was promoted to chair professor at this university.<ref name="biography"/>

In 1993 he organized the workshop ''Continuous Algorithms and Complexity'' at the [[Centre de Recerca Matemàtica]] in Barcelona<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.crm.cat/en/Host/SciEvents/ConfWk/Documents/PastConferences.pdf|title=Past Events before 2011|website=[[Centre de Recerca Matemàtica]]|access-date=2020-10-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002163445/http://www.crm.cat/en/Host/SciEvents/ConfWk/Documents/PastConferences.pdf|archive-date=2020-10-02}}</ref><ref>{{citation
 | title = Selected papers of the Workshop on Continuous Algorithms and Complexity. Theoret. Comput. Sci.
 | editor-last = Cucker
 | editor-first = Felipe
 | volume = 113
 | publisher = Elsevier
 | year = 1994 | issue = 1
 }}</ref> where he started his long-term collaboration with [[Lenore Blum]], [[Michael Shub]], and [[Steve Smale]].<ref name="biography"/> In 1996 he moved with them to the [[City University of Hong Kong]] to write the book [[Complexity and Real Computation]].<ref name="interview"/><ref name="biography"/> Although this was intended as a temporal position,<ref name="biography"/> Cucker would stay in Hong Kong and became an [[associate professor]] of this university in 1998, [[full professor]] in 2003, and chair professor in 2006.<ref name="arbol"/>

Cucker was one of the founders of the nonprofit association [[Foundations of Computational Mathematics]], of which he has been a member of the board of directors since its creation in 1995 until 2017. Additionally, Cucker was Chair of this society from 2008 to 2011 and Editor-in-Chief of its journal from 2011 to 2017.<ref name="arbol"/><ref>{{cite web|access-date=2020-10-05|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/na/FoCM/Governance.html|title=Governance of FoCM (2001-02-02)|publisher=[[Foundations of Computational Mathematics]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010202215700/http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/na/FoCM/Governance.html|archive-date=2001-02-02}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://focm-society.org/governance.php|access-date=2020-10-05|title=Governance of FoCM|publisher=[[Foundations of Computational Mathematics]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200217095537/http://focm-society.org/governance.php|archive-date=2020-02-17}} See also:
* {{cite web|url=http://focm-society.org/governance_2014-2017.php|title=Governance of FoCM, 2014–2017|access-date=2020-10-05|publisher=[[Foundations of Computational Mathematics]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200218010113/http://focm-society.org/governance_2014-2017.php|archive-date=2020-02-18}}
* {{cite web|url=http://focm-society.org/governance_2011-2014.php|title=Governance of FoCM, 2011–2014|access-date=2020-10-05|publisher=[[Foundations of Computational Mathematics]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200218005820/http://focm-society.org/governance_2011-2014.php|archive-date=2020-02-18}}
* {{cite web|url=http://focm-society.org/governance_2008-2011.php|title=Governance of FoCM, 2008–2011|access-date=2020-10-05|publisher=[[Foundations of Computational Mathematics]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200218005812/http://focm-society.org/governance_2008-2011.php|archive-date=2020-02-18}}</ref>

In 2006 Cucker was named foreign member of the [[Royal Academy of Sciences and Arts of Barcelona]].<ref name="arbol"/><ref>{{citation|url=https://www.racab.cat/en/?view=category&id=102|title=Foreign Members of the Royal Academy of Sciences and Arts of Barcelona|publisher=[[Royal Academy of Sciences and Arts of Barcelona]]|access-date=2020-10-02}}.</ref>

From 2017 to 2019 Cucker was Einstein Visiting Fellow of the [[Berlin Mathematical School]] and [[Technische Universität Berlin]].<ref name="biography"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math-berlin.de/media-press/news/fellowships-offered-by-new-einstein-visiting-fellow|title=Fellowships offered by new Einstein Visiting Fellow|access-date=2020-10-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180419183933/https://www.math-berlin.de/media-press/news/fellowships-offered-by-new-einstein-visiting-fellow|archive-date=2018-04-19}}</ref>

In 2019, the conference ''Complexity of numerical computation: A conference in honor of Felipe Cucker'' was organised at the [[Technische Universität Berlin]] in Berlin celebrating his work.<ref>''[http://felipesfest.github.io//index.html Complexity of numerical computation: A conference in honor of Felipe Cucker]''</ref>

Since 2018 he is Head of the Mathematics Department at [[City University of Hong Kong]].<ref name="biography"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cityu.edu.hk/ma/people/fac.htm|title=MA Academic Faculty of the City University of Hong Kong|access-date=2020-10-02|date=18 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200303055005/https://www.cityu.edu.hk/ma/people/fac.htm|archive-date=2020-03-03}}.</ref>

== Work ==

During the 90s, he worked in the complexity classes that appear when dealing with the [[Blum–Shub–Smale machine]]. In 1998, he co-authored one of the fundamental books in this topic, ''[[Complexity and Real Computation]]'', together with [[Lenore Blum]], [[Michael Shub]], and [[Steve Smale]].<ref name="arbol"/>

In the 2000s he focused on the analysis of numerical algorithms in linear programming. Together with Dennis Cheung he introduced the notions of the GCC condition number in linear programming.<ref>{{cite journal
|last1=Hauser
|first1=Raphael
|last2=Müller
|first2=Tobias
|title=Conditioning of random conic systems under a general family of input distributions
|journal= Foundations of Computational Mathematics
|volume=9
|date=2009
|number=3
|pages=335–358
|issn=1615-3375
|mr=2496555
|doi=10.1007/s10208-008-9034-0
|s2cid=16493721
}}</ref>

In 2007 together with [[Steve Smale]] he proposed the so-called Cucker-Smale flocking model. This model, which has received extensive attention in mathematics and other fields,<ref>
{{cite journal
|last1=Figalli
|first1=Alessio
|author1-link=Alessio Figalli
|last2=Kang
|first2=Moon-Jin
|title=A rigorous derivation from the kinetic Cucker-Smale model to the pressureless Euler system with nonlocal alignment
|journal= Analysis & PDE
|volume=12
|date=2019
|number=3
|pages=843–866
|issn=2157-5045
|mr=3864212
|doi=10.2140/apde.2019.12.843
|arxiv=1702.08087
|s2cid=119604972
}}
</ref> plays an important role in the mathematical study of [[Flocking (behavior)|flocking dynamics]].<ref name="arbol"/><ref>
{{cite journal
|title=Collective motion
|last1=Vicsek
|first1=Tamás
|author1-link=Tamás Vicsek
|last2=Zafeiris
|first2=Anna
|journal=Physics Reports
|volume=517
|number=3–4
|pages=71–140
|year=2012
|doi=10.1016/j.physrep.2012.03.004
|arxiv=1010.5017
|bibcode=2012PhR...517...71V
|s2cid=119109873
}}
</ref>

In 2011 together with [[Peter Bürgisser]] he contributed to the solution of [[Smale's problems|Smale's 17th problem]].<ref name="arbol"/>

In 2013 Cucker won an Honorable Mention in the Category of Mathematics of the [[PROSE Awards]] for his book ''Manifold Mirrors: The Crossing Paths of the Arts and Mathematics'', which dealt with [[mathematics and art]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://proseawards.com/winners/2013-award-winners/|title=2013 Winners of the PROSE Awards|access-date=2020-10-05|publisher=[[Association of American Publishers]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190426194606/https://proseawards.com/winners/2013-award-winners/|archive-date=2019-04-26}}</ref>
